findings.evidence: SemisimplePoint.lean:7 is the sole import; lines 73-171 mention no `Tannaka.` declaration, while the first `Tannaka.` reference is at line 177. `grep '^namespace' Tannaka/*.lean` gives `TauCeti.Tannaka` for all eight pre-existing files.
findings.fix: Move the definition through `IsSemisimplePoint.mul_of_commute` into `TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/SemisimplePoint.lean` (importing `Representation.PointsAction` and `LinearAlgebra.JordanChevalley.Multiplicative`), and keep only `isSemisimplePoint_iff_fgPointSemisimplePartNatIso_eq_fgPointNatIsoHom` in the Tannaka file.
findings.issue: `IsSemisimplePoint` and its whole closure API (lines 73-171) use no Tannakian material — only `Comodule.pointsAction` (Representation/PointsAction.lean), `FGComoduleCat` (Coalgebra/Comodule/Finite/Basic.lean) and `GeneralLinearGroup.IsSemisimple` — yet they sit in `Representation/Tannaka/` behind `import ...Tannaka.JordanDecomposition`, so any consumer of the predicate must pull in the Tannakian scalar-extension-functor machinery. The namespace also breaks the directory convention: every other file in `Tannaka/` opens `namespace TauCeti.Tannaka`, this one opens `namespace TauCeti.HopfAlgebra`.

summary: Three placement problems: a pure ring-theory lemma parked under LinearAlgebra/GeneralLinearGroup, unrelated general-linear-group coercion lemmas in a file named Adjoin.lean, and the non-Tannakian semisimple-point definition plus its closure API buried in the Tannaka subdirectory behind an import of the Tannakian Jordan decomposition.
